title: Framed rack with multiple vertical panels, tubing and valve assemblies in a workshop
objects_and_counts: No people are visible in the photographed scene.
Five large rectangular front-facing panels with vertical yellow strips are visible along the long side of a rectangular metal frame; the leftmost panel is partially cropped by the image edge.
A bolted perforated orange-brown metal frame supports the panels; the frame spans the length of the visible panels and has horizontal top rails and vertical supports.

Multiple clear plastic tubes emerge from the bottom edge of the panels and run downward and to the right; an exact tube count cannot be reliably determined from this view but at least a dozen distinct tube ends are visibly grouped beneath the panels.
Two vertical cylindrical assemblies with flanged joints and red-handled valves are visible at the lower-left foreground (they appear mounted together in a vertical stack).
One small two-step metal/wooden stool is positioned at front-right next to the frame.
Three stacked blue rectangular box units are visible at left rear of the frame (stacked vertically).
One blue vertical ladder is visible behind the frame, roughly centered in the image.
One flexible yellow corrugated duct or hose is visible at the top-right background, curving downward.
One grey desk lamp is mounted on the top rail of the frame toward the center-back.
A grey curtain or drape is visible in the mid-background behind the frame; a tripod or camera-like object is visible near that curtain.
spatial_relations: The long side of the orange-brown perforated metal frame faces the camera; the five rectangular panels are mounted vertically along this front face of the frame.
The clear plastic tubes are connected to or exit from the bottom edge of the panels and hang down beneath the frame, then run to the right and under the frame.
The two vertical cylindrical valve assemblies with red handles sit to the front-left of the frame and are connected near the leftmost region of the visible equipment.
The three blue box units are positioned to the rear-left of the frame, sitting on a surface behind the left end of the frame.
The small two-step stool is placed on the floor directly in front of and slightly to the right of the frame, adjacent to the rightmost panels.
A blue ladder rises behind the center of the frame, with the ladder base behind the frame and its top extending above the frame.
A grey lamp is located on the top rail of the frame toward the center-back, pointing over the panels.
A curtain hangs in the mid-background behind the frame; a tripod-like object is placed in front of that curtain.
colours_and_materials: The vertical strips on the rectangular panels are yellow against a brown or tan backing board.
The supporting structure is an orange-brown perforated metal (possibly painted steel) with visible bolt holes.
Clear/transparent plastic tubing is visible beneath the panels.
The floor is a blue painted surface, and there is a black textured anti-slip mat in front of the frame.
The stacked boxes at left are blue; a corrugated flexible duct at top-right is yellow.
The stool appears to have a grey top surface and an orange-brown perforated metal frame matching the main support frame.
uncertainties: No fully legible text was found; a small warning sign and small handwritten marks or labels appear in the background and on panel edges but the characters are unreadable at this resolution ([unreadable]).
Exact count of clear plastic tubes is uncertain because many overlap and some are occluded; 'at least a dozen' is a conservative visible minimum.
The leftmost rectangular panel is partially cropped by the image edge, so the total number of panels in the assembly could be greater than the five visible.
The function and exact type of the rectangular panels (e.g., filter, electrode, circuit board) cannot be determined from appearance alone and are not asserted here.
No room name or number is visible in the image; the facility or building affiliation cannot be determined from the photograph.
